s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of a painless swelling over a pacemaker site with a soft tissue mass and increased vascularity surrounding the device
salient_findings: Painless swelling over the pacemaker site
Soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the device on chest ultrasound
CT imaging confirmed a soft-tissue mass around the pacemaker pocket
key_facts: 70-year-old man with a history of nicotine use
Remote history of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Remote history of bladder urothelial carcinoma
Dual-chamber pacemaker implantation for sick sinus syndrome 9 months prior
Postoperative checks showed normal pacemaker function and a clinically unremarkable pocket
Tested positive for COVID-19 infection 3 weeks before presentation
Fatigue, dyspnea, and cough persisted and worsened after COVID-19 infection
New swelling over the pacemaker site reported at a routine cardiology visit
Normal blood pressure and heart rate on examination
No signs of cardiac decompensation or cachexia
Haematoma or infection was excluded by imaging

shortlist.why_kept: History of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma and new swelling over pacemaker site

shortlist.label: Metastatic bladder urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of bladder urothelial carcinoma and new swelling over pacemaker site

shortlist.label: Pacemaker pocket sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: New swelling over pacemaker site with soft tissue mass and increased vascularity

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the device

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms such as fatigue, dyspnea, and cough, and new swelling over pacemaker site

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of pacemaker implantation and presents with a new, painless swelling over the pacemaker site, which was found to be a soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the device. This is consistent with a pacemaker pocket sarcoma, a rare but recognized complication of pacemaker implantation.

rejected.label: Metastatic laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's history of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma is remote (7 years prior), making metastasis less likely

rejected.label: Metastatic bladder urothelial carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's history of bladder urothelial carcinoma is also remote (10 years prior), making metastasis less likely

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: While angiosarcoma is a type of sarcoma, the presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with a pacemaker pocket sarcoma

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence to suggest lymphoma, such as lymphadenopathy or systemic symptoms
